newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Schroeder - soft euro would damage trust.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Schroeder - soft euro would damage trust.

text.p: Gerhard Schroeder, a leading challenger to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, said on Wednesday relaxing the fiscal criteria for Europe's planned single currency would damage public confidence in the project.
Schroeder, a leader in the Social Democrats (SPD) also told MDR radio that he disagreed with those who fear that delaying the single European currency would be tantamount to scrapping the project.

"If the will to introduce it is only there for a certain date then that shows there is not enough will anyhow," Schroeder said. "The will has to be permanently there. One cannot put forth this argument for what may possibly be a necessary delay."
Schroeder, the premier of Lower Saxony and a well-known euro-sceptic, said the German government had promised the public that the single European currency would be a stable currency.
